To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

subjects divide a sequence of actions into more units when the sequence begins unpredictably than when the sequence begins predictably, when the pattern of the sequence changes, and when the sequence is unpredictable.
the predictability of behavior has an important effect on both how people partition behavior into units of action, and how they attribute causality to behavior.

subjects divide an actor's behavior into a larger number of units when (1) the behavior begins unpredictably than when the behavior begins predictably and (2) when the pattern changes from predictable to unpredictable or from unpredictable to predictable than when the pattern remains the same.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of varying the predictabil-ity of a social actor's behavior upon (a) the manner in which an observer partitions the actor's behavior and (b) the causal attributions the observer makes for the actor's behavior.
how people divide social information into units of perception.
the effects of varying predictability of behavior upon the manner and extent to which observers divide it into units and attribute causality to the actor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more predictable an action is, the more likely it is to be perceived as a single unit, and the more likely it will be perceived as caused by internal factors.
predictability of an observed actor's behavior affects both how the observer perceives the behavior and the observer's causal attributions for it.
the more predictable a behavior, the fewer the units of action and the more dispositional the causal attributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

people tend to divide a behavior into more units when they are uncertain about the causes of that behavior, and that they make dispositional attributions for behavior when the behavior is divided into more units. (Author/DB)
